# MKL Flash Attention Workflow

## Project Layout
- **Build area**: `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\llama.cpp` (source + build dir)
- **Build output**: `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\llama.cpp\build-x64-windows-sycl-release\bin\llama-server.exe`
- **Scripts**: `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\scripts\` (mkl-build.bat, mkl-server.bat, mkl-test.sh)
- **Logs**: `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\logs\`
- **Daily driver**: `C:\llama.cpp-prod\` (models, prompts, benchmark results)
- **Models**: `C:\llama.cpp-prod\models\presets\`
- **Prompts**: `C:\llama.cpp-prod\docs\Prompts.txt`
- **Bench results**: `C:\llama.cpp-prod\docs\`

## GPU
Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage BMG-G21, 32GB VRAM)

## Build
```bash
source /c/llama.cpp-build-sycl/scripts/mkl-test.sh
mkl-build              # incremental
mkl-build --configure  # full reconfigure + build
```
Under the hood: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 cmd.exe /c "C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\scripts\mkl-build.bat"`

## Key Source Files
- `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-sycl\fattn-mkl.cpp` — MKL FA kernel (the main file)
- `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-sycl\fattn-common.hpp` — TILE reference kernel
- `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-sycl\fattn.cpp` — kernel dispatch + FA-DIAG output fingerprint
- `C:\llama.cpp-build-sycl\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-sycl\convert.cpp` — dequantization implementations

## Environment Variables
- `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_MKL_FA=1` (default, MKL enabled) / `0` (TILE fallback)
- `GGML_SYCL_MKL_FA_DEBUG=1` — FA-DISP watchdog: log n_kv deltas per FA call
- `GGML_SYCL_MKL_FA_DIAG=1` — FA-DIAG: dump first 64 output floats for cross-kernel comparison (see fattn.cpp)
- `SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=0`, `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0`

## Model Aliases
| Alias | Model File | Tokenizer |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| Qwen27B | Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL.gguf | Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B |
| Qwen35B | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf | Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B |
| Gemma26B | gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-UD-Q5_K_M.gguf | google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it |
| Gemma31B | gemma-4-31B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf | google/gemma-4-31B-it |

## Common Commands
```bash
source /c/llama.cpp-build-sycl/scripts/mkl-test.sh

# Build
mkl-build

# Quick coherence check on one model
mkl-smoke Qwen27B

# Benchmark MKL vs TILE at 32K
mkl-compare Qwen27B 32768 512

# Full validation on all models
mkl-test-all
```

## Critical Detail: `sizeof(sycl::half)`
oneAPI has `sizeof(sycl::half) == 2` on this platform (confirmed). Device fp16 is always 2 bytes. When reading device fp16 buffers, use raw `uint16_t` and manual fp16→f32 conversion, or `unsigned short`, to avoid host-side alignment issues.

## Fixed Bug: dst interleaved layout
The MKL normalize kernel was writing dst output in dense head-major format when llama.cpp expects interleaved `(query * n_heads + head) * DV`. Fixed in `mkl_fa_normalize_head`. This is the ONLY line that changed for the actual fix — everything else was debug diagnostics.

## Server Kill
```bash
taskkill //f //im llama-server.exe
```

**Why:** When `mkl-coherence` returns a response but not a good one, see [[mkl-fa-bug-dst-layout]].

**How to apply:** Source `mkl-test.sh` in bash, then use the short function names listed above. For new models, add entries to both `mkl-server.bat` (alias → path) and `mkl-test.sh` (tokenizer mapping).

## Problem: The two `git checkout` commands

You can't be on two branches at once. The second `git checkout heartbeat-no-sleep` **throws away** the first checkout of `sycl-mkl-flash-attn`. You end up with only `heartbeat-no-sleep`'s changes.

## Fix

You need to combine them. The simplest approach — create a combined branch with both PRs on top of latest master:

```batch
git fetch origin master
git checkout -b combined-sycl-mkl-heartbeat origin/master
git merge sycl-mkl-flash-attn
git merge heartbeat-no-sleep
```

Or if you prefer one PR rebased on top of the other (and both on latest master):

```batch
git fetch origin master
git checkout sycl-mkl-flash-attn
git rebase origin/master
git merge heartbeat-no-sleep
```


- `-DGGML_SYCL_DEVICE_ARCH=bmg_g21` — correct for your Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage BMG-G21)

1. `git fetch origin master` - This doesn't "clear out everything." It downloads the latest master branch from GitHub (the remote called `origin`) into your local copy. It doesn't modify your working files at all.

If you then run `git push` (which would push `sycl-mkl-flash-attn` to origin), it would push the combined code to the `sycl-mkl-flash-attn` branch on GitHub — NOT to `heartbeat-no-sleep`. The heartbeat branch remains untouched. The push goes to whichever branch you're currently on.

content.text:
Close, but a couple of corrections that matter:

## What each command actually does

| Command | Reality |
|---|---|
| `git fetch origin master` | Downloads the latest master **without touching your working files**. Doesn't clear anything. |
| `git checkout sycl-mkl-flash-attn` | Switches to your **local** branch of that name. No download — it was already on your machine. |
| `git rebase origin/master` | Replays your MKL FA commits so they sit **on top of** the latest master commits (cleaner history). |
| `git merge heartbeat-no-sleep` | Merges the heartbeat branch into your current branch. |

## And the push question

If you ran `git push` while on `sycl-mkl-flash-attn`, it would push the combined code **to `sycl-mkl-flash-attn` on GitHub** — not to `heartbeat-no-sleep`.

`git push` pushes the current branch to its upstream counterpart. The heartbeat branch stays untouched. You'd be updating your MKL FA PR (if that branch is tied to one) with heartbeat code, which you probably don't want.

So the rule is simple: **just don't `git push`** and you're safe. Build, test, delete the branch when you're done — nothing leaves your machine.

content.text:
Good instinct to be paranoid. Here's the cleanest workflow:

## The safe way: disposable integration branch

Create a **throwaway** branch just for building and testing:

```batch
git checkout -b test-mkl-heartbeat
git rebase origin/master       # you're already on sycl-mkl-flash-attn though...
```

Actually, let me back up. Based on what you already did, you're on `sycl-mkl-flash-attn` with heartbeat merged in. To get truly safe going forward:

```batch
# 1. Create a disposable integration branch from where you are now
git checkout -b test-mkl-heartbeat

# 2. Switch back to clean MKL branch (undo the merge)
git checkout sycl-mkl-flash-attn
git reset --hard origin/sycl-mkl-flash-attn   # or wherever it was before the merge
```

Now you have:
- `test-mkl-heartbeat` — the combined Frankenstein you build and test (never pushed, never leave changes here)
- `sycl-mkl-flash-attn` — clean, only MKL code (safe to push)
- `heartbeat-no-sleep` — clean, only heartbeat code (safe to push)

## When you need to fix heartbeat

```batch
# Fix it on the REAL heartbeat branch
git checkout heartbeat-no-sleep
# ... make your changes ...
git commit -m "fix: whatever"
git push   # clean push — no MKL code here

# Then pull the fix into your test branch
git checkout test-mkl-heartbeat
git merge heartbeat-no-sleep
# rebuild, retest
```

## The mental model

```
sycl-mkl-flash-attn  ────●───●───●   (push only this to MKL PR)
heartbeat-no-sleep    ────●───●───●   (push only this to heartbeat PR)
test-mkl-heartbeat    ────●──●──●──   (never push, throw away when done)
                            /\
                           /  \
                     merges from both parent branches
```

The key rule: **never commit on the test branch**. All real work happens on the original branches, and you just merge them into the test branch to rebuild. When both PRs are merged upstream, delete `test-mkl-heartbeat` and it's like it never existed.
